title: Leader Dots and Boxed Formatting
pattern: Comments using special padding strings like leader dots, boxed border lines, or column alignment markers.
why_bad: Maintenance trap. Modifying or adding a variable requires manual adjustment of all adjacent padding characters. Developers will avoid updating comments to bypass the tedious formatting work, causing comments to go stale.
detection: Inline comments containing long chains of dots (`...`), lines of dashes, or pluses (`+-------+`) used for vertical key-value alignment.
counterexample: Plain unaligned one-line comments ('// x_pos - X coordinate position (meters)') that need no padding maintenance.
fix: Format comments as standard paragraphs or simple clean lists with no padding alignments.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Java Example of a Commenting Style That's Hard to Maintain").
